card.author: day-audit
card.title: Rename the assistant skill to every-prompt (re-invoked on every prompt), updating every reference; add the two-tier design: a fast Sonnet assistant and a master assistant that receives every prompt after the relay.
card.why: Renamed, both tiers defined, every reference updated, and the old command path kept as a forwarder so nothing in flight broke. Checked: the skill exists and the old assistant skill is gone.
card.done: Renamed, with both tiers defined; every reference updated, both names accepted by the hooks, and the old command path kept as a forwarder so nothing in flight broke.
card.quote: RENAME the assistant skill to 'every-prompt' (same content and setup carried over; the skill is meant to re-invoke on every prompt). [...] Add a two-tier design to the skill: a FAST assistant (Sonnet) that echoes, writes cards and relays instantly, and a MASTER assistant (Fable) that receives every prompt after the fast one relays it.
card.said: Make sure it's very clear to use the skill on every prompt. So every time I send a new message, that skill is invoked. It re-reads. So maybe the every prompt skill itself should be kept minimal. If there are lengthy instructions, if we need sub skills essentially, then you can have additional readmes in the skill. The every prompt skill could identify any number of sub readmes and give an overview of when you would need to use it, and then just say load this file and read it if you need to do this or this. Those could be on every task or decision or whatever. So we could have different types of sub skills there. But the idea is that if it's loading this on every single prompt, we don't want to overload the skill with unnecessary detail. The general idea is that first, every prompt verbatim goes to the master assistant. And maybe we create a separate skill called master assistant, maybe it can be a sub skill, I don't care about that. The master assistant is going to just supervise, overlook what's going on and be aware of what's going on. If the fast assistant needs feedback, he can ask the master assistant. The master assistant can automatically reply, I suppose. We don't want it to do a bunch of work. It's really just there to give feedback, to give opinions, like don't forget to do this, I don't think you should be doing that that way, whatever. And the master assistant should probably document on some page somewhere that whole process and how it's going. Maybe the master assistant could also be the skill auditor, the system auditor, because that would be a good role for him, to pay attention to everything and think about the design of the system and whether it's working.

card.why: every-prompt is a third of its old size with load-this-if files, and a master-assistant skill exists that supervises, opines, documents the process and audits. Checked: both skills are on disk.

card.quote: the every-prompt skill stays minimal and re-reads on every prompt; long detail lives in sub-readmes it names with 'load this if you need X' [...] A separate MASTER ASSISTANT skill or sub-skill: it only supervises and knows what is going on; the fast assistant can ask it for feedback, and it can reply automatically with opinions [...] It documents the whole process and how it is going on a page, and doubles as the SYSTEM/skill auditor. [...] Assistants do no deep reasoning; they sort, log everything that can be logged, and relay each prompt to the proper independent mastermind.
card.said: All right, so the fast assistant with the help maybe of the master assistant can work together to keep the UI updated quickly. And the system auditor, we want to figure out how, we want to measure the timing of everything, from the time the prompt gets there to the time the UI gets updated, all the timing. And that should happen on the timeline generally, so it's all visual. Then the assistants can spawn masterminds. I think what the fast assistant can learn to do is relay the prompt to the proper mastermind. And the mastermind is a little bit slower, so it's going to take a minute to get the proper feedback, but the more we can offload to independent masterminds that are doing the deep reasoning and maybe spawning minions for parallelization. We want to build this into the right skill system, for the right roles. But I do think having these assistants that are not doing any deep reasoning, they're just sorting the messages essentially and deciding when to use their skills. So logging, everything that can be logged should be logged. The prompt that comes in gets logged immediately. We transform it, kind of summarize it, but I think maybe what I want to do is approve
